messages:
devon: heads up: new int8 onboard (sable-liteq) in canary shows ~5.6% funcall parse failures, baseline fp32 is 0.2%. mostly streaming toolcalls. :confused:
maya: any repro artifacts? truncated json or weird bytes?
devon: got a few dumps. example chunk sequence: 
```
...}\u0000\u001e{"name":"open","args":{...}}
```
aj: 0x00 + RS (0x1E) will definitely trip our NDJSON parser. looks like tokenization/emit changed with quant path so boundaries hit inside escape/close sequences.
maya: quick mitigation: add a streaming sanitizer that replaces lone RS/NULL with newline and buffers until a full top-level object is available. emit a repair metric for visibility. keep this behind a canary flag.
aj: pseudo: 
```
buf += chunk
buf = buf.replace('\u0000','\n').replace('\u001e','\n')
while has_complete_object(buf): emit(parse(next_object)); buf = remainder
```
devon: agree but log every repair. we must not mask corrupted payloads silently. ops-bot: created ticket INF-3220 "stream-sanitize + token-trace for int8 canary" and attached current dumps.
maya: I'll ship a non-invasive sanitizer PR today; aj can orchestrate a 50/50 canary split tomorrow. if repair_rate > 1% we escalate to runtime kernel team for deeper investigation.
canary-bot: scheduled canary 630888 for 08:00 PT tomorrow. good luck :rocket:
